newsitem.title: CONGO: Seven new Ebola virus deaths in Gabon - WHO.
newsitem.headline: Seven new Ebola virus deaths in Gabon - WHO.

text.p: A new outbreak of the Ebola virus has killed seven people in Gabon, the World Health Organisation's regional headquarters in Congo said on Friday.
The seven died in hospital last Saturday in the town of Boue, in Ogoue Province east of Libreville, said Dr Andre Ndikauyeze, WHO's epidemiologist in charge of surveillance in the area.
At least 13 people died in the area last February in an outbreak of Ebola, which is marked by fever, vomitting, diarrhoea and massive bleeding and kills most of its victims.
Health officials said then the virus broke out from among families who ate or handled dead chimpanzees in the remote area.
Ndikauyeze told reporters the number of cases in the latest outbreak were not yet known but 27 people, including relatives and health workers, had come in contact with the dead.
Ebola is transmitted by direct contact with blood secretions or body fluids.
The virus struck in Kikwit, Zaire in May 1995, killing 245 people -- a 77 percent fatality. A single victim in Ivory Coast last December survived.
